title: Lost-wax cast aluminum wordlines replace CVD tungsten
idea: Like investment casting: fill buried-wordline trenches with a carbon 'wax' placeholder through all high-temperature steps, burn it out with an oxygen-radical ash, then squeeze-cast molten Al-Si-Sc alloy into the voids at ~600 C and high pressure over the TiN gate liner and planarize.
why: Removes WF6 and tungsten (China ~80%) from the densest metal layer in the array and cuts wordline resistance ~1.5-2x, which allows thinner wordlines; uses the most abundant structural metal and no fluorinated precursor.

title: Eliminate ESD and I/O drivers: protection-free hybrid-bonded memory pins
idea: When DRAM is wafer-bonded to logic and never handled as a bare die, delete the ESD diodes, thick-oxide drivers and termination on every data pin and drive ~50 fF bond pads at 0.4 V from core devices.
why: ESD and pad capacitance dominate I/O energy; pin energy falls from pJ to ~10-50 fJ per bit (>10x), and I/O periphery area (fact 7) shrinks.

title: Catalytic-converter-style smelting recovers tungsten from fab chamber waste
idea: Adapted from autocatalyst PGM recycling, which combines a collection network, assay-based pricing and smelt-and-refine. Collect W-coated chamber shields, spent W sputter targets and WF6 abatement scrubber sludge, oxidize them, refine via ammonium paratungstate and refluorinate to WF6 domestically.
why: Tungsten is ~80% Chinese, and CVD W uses only a small fraction of the delivered WF6; the rest ends up in abatement. Recovering 30-50% of fab tungsten flows creates a domestic secondary supply.

title: Graphene liner lets copper fill the buried wordline
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out: grow a 1-2 layer graphene diffusion barrier in the wordline trench by low-temperature plasma CVD, then fill with Cu. A ~0.4 nm barrier replaces ~3 nm of TiN, and Cu, the lowest-resistivity abundant metal, replaces W.
why: ~3x lower wordline resistance than TiN/W at ~10 nm width allows faster or lower-voltage wordlines (fact 10), with no W. Uses only C and Cu, plus Si and O.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching digs 150:1 capacitor holes without plasma
idea: Magnify aspect ratio while shrinking gas use to zero: a perforated Ag or Pt catalyst film immersed in HF/H2O2 sinks vertically into silicon, carving 150:1 holes with no fluorocarbon plasma, RF power or helium-cooled chuck. The silicon walls are then oxidized into the capacitor scaffold.
why: Removes C4F6/C4F8 PFAS etch gases and the hardest etch tool from the cell. AR 150 vs 70 roughly doubles Cs (fact 1).

title: Urban-mined tungsten: carbide scrap to domestic WF6 loop
idea: Inverts 'tungsten comes from mines (China ~80%)': dedicate US cemented-carbide scrap recycling (zinc-process and oxidation routes) to APT and then WF6 for fabs, and feed fab chamber scrapings and spent targets back into the same loop under long-term offtake contracts.
why: A few hundred tonnes per year of domestic scrap can cover US fab WF6 demand, insulating DRAM from tungsten export controls and price shocks.

title: Phosphate-fertilizer fluorosilicic acid becomes domestic electronic-grade HF
idea: Florida phosphate plants scrub fluorosilicic acid (H2SiF6) out as a waste stream. Adapt the fertilizer industry's FSA-to-fluoride routes to crack FSA into anhydrous HF, then distill it to ppt-grade for wafer etch and for NF3/WF6 synthesis.
why: HF depends on fluorspar (China ~60%). US phosphate by-product fluorine could cover domestic fab HF demand, removing a mining chokepoint.

title: Dish soap: sugar-based surfactants replace PFAS in oxide etchants
idea: Stimulus 'dish soap' -> a 10-person chemical team formulates alkyl-polyglucoside/siloxane surfactants that drop the surface tension of buffered HF and developers enough to wet 60:1 holes, replacing fluorosurfactants in BOE and wet-clean chemistries.
why: Removes PFAS from DRAM wet chemistry ahead of bans using sugar-derived feedstock; small-batch blending.

title: Single stitch-metal mask harvests independent quarter-dies at wafer edge
idea: Combine a tiled die with wafer-edge recovery: the die is built as four self-sufficient quadrants, and the one added top-metal stitch mask ties them into a full die in complete fields while edge partial fields are left as independent quarter-capacity dies.
why: Recovers ~3-6% more bits per wafer from edge silicon now scrapped, equivalently less wafer, crucible and energy per bit.

title: Molten-salt electro-deoxidation turns quartz sand into silicon near thermodynamic minimum
idea: Reducing SiO2 to Si needs a minimum of ~9 kWh/kg while the Siemens chlorosilane route uses 50-100. Press SiO2 into cathodes, electro-deoxidize in molten CaCl2 at 850 C (FFC route), then reach 11N with a float-zone pass, skipping trichlorosilane, HCl and H2.
why: Polysilicon energy down ~4-5x and the chlorosilane chemical chain removed; reaching electronic-grade purity is the risk.

title: Substitute amorphous-carbon molds and ashing for oxide mold HF dip-out
idea: Build the capacitor mold from amorphous carbon etched with O2/COS (no fluorocarbons), form the pillars, then remove the mold by O2/H2 plasma ash instead of a buffered-HF full dip-out followed by rinses and IPA drying.
why: Deletes the wet dip-out, cutting capacitor-module water >10x; with no liquid meniscus, pillars can exceed AR 100 without leaning (charge wall), and the etch is PFAS-free.

title: Oxygen-ashable carbon mold capacitors with no HF dip-out
idea: Imposed scarcity: no fluorocarbon gases and no HF. Build the capacitor mold from amorphous carbon etched in O2/N2/COS plasma, deposit TiN/ZAZ at <=400 C, then remove the mold by O2 ashing instead of an HF wet dip-out.
why: Removes PFC etch gases and the wet capillary forces that topple tall pillars, so AR can rise from ~70 toward ~100 for more Cs; also cuts PFAS-regulated chemistry and UPW per wafer.

title: HVAC hydrogen-tracer leak testing eliminates helium mass-spec checks
idea: Refrigeration and automotive A/C lines are leak-checked with non-flammable 5% H2 / 95% N2 tracer and solid-state sniffers. Requalify fab vacuum-chamber, gas-line and package-hermeticity testing to H2 tracer with residual-gas analyzers tuned to mass 2; nothing changes in the DDR/HBM product.
why: Leak checking is a significant non-cooling helium use; switching removes it entirely using forming gas made anywhere, easing the helium chokepoint.

title: Eliminate NF3 cleans: closed fluorine loop with on-site electrolytic F2
idea: Scrub HF from fab exhaust and wet benches, electrolyze it as KF-2HF on site to regenerate F2 for chamber cleaning, and retire purchased NF3 (GWP ~17,000).
why: Cuts dependence on fluorspar (China-dominated) and on concentrated NF3 makers, and removes a potent greenhouse emission.

title: Molybdenum-disulfide access transistors grown from domestic molybdenum
idea: Minify the channel to three atoms: grow MoS2 monolayers by low-temperature MOCVD from US-mined Mo and sulfur as access transistors. Their 1.8-2 eV gap and lack of junctions keep leakage below 1e-18 A/um at 125 C.
why: Long retention at temperature without the indium or gallium of wide-gap oxides; BEOL-compatible for 3D stacking; both elements are abundant and domestic.

title: Water-soluble salt release layer for stacking oxide memory tiers
idea: Periodic-table walk, Na+Cl (11,17): evaporate a NaCl film on a reusable carrier, seal it with ALD Al2O3, build an oxide-transistor DRAM tier at <=400 C (below NaCl's 801 C melt), bond it onto the stack, and dissolve the salt in water to release it.
why: Tier-by-tier 3D DRAM without HF/XeF2 sacrificial release and without consuming a Si wafer per tier; carrier reused indefinitely.

title: Mandatory second-sourcing revived for a no-EUV American DRAM process
idea: Revive the 1960s-80s defense rule that every critical chip has a licensed second source: require CHIPS-funded DRAM designs to be built on an open no-EUV process licensed to at least two US mature-node foundries.
why: U.S. manufacturability and resilience: spreads output across existing DUV capacity and avoids the single-supplier EUV chokepoint.

title: Eliminate refresh and capacitors: complementary oxide-TFT static latch cell
idea: Build a cross-coupled latch from n-type Zn-Sn-O and p-type SnO thin-film transistors stacked in the BEOL; wide-gap off-current near 1e-19 A means the static cell draws almost nothing yet never needs refresh, and reads non-destructively at ~100 mV differential swing.
why: Removes the capacitor, the 46 fJ/bit refresh and the restore step; low-swing non-destructive reads are ~10x cheaper, using only abundant elements.

title: Gallium-free zinc-tin-silicon oxide channels for low-leak gain cells
idea: Oxide gain cells leak little because Eg>3 eV makes intrinsic carriers ~1e-25 cm-3 and holes immobile; mobility comes from overlapping metal ns orbitals, which Sn4+ 5s supplies as well as In3+, while Si (strong Si-O bond) takes Ga's carrier-suppressing role. Deposit amorphous Zn-Sn-Si-O by ALD as read and write channels.
why: Removes gallium (China ~98%, export-controlled) and indium from IGZO gain-cell roadmaps while keeping sub-aA off-current; Zn and Si are abundant and US-sourced.

title: Silicon-carbide DRAM: refresh-free at 125 C, grown without quartz
idea: Magnify bandgap ~3x: build 1T1C cells in 4H-SiC, whose junction leakage at 125 C is ~10^10 below silicon's, on boules grown by sublimation in graphite crucibles, so no high-purity quartz crucible is needed.
why: Hours of retention at 125 C remove refresh energy (fact 3) for automotive and industrial memory, and avoid the HPQ and CZ chokepoints; SiC substrate lines already run in North Carolina and New York.

title: Spall, don't grind: peel HBM dies off reusable parents
idea: Reverse thinning: instead of grinding a 775 um wafer down to 40 um for HBM, deposit a nickel stressor and controlled-spall the 40 um device layer off, then re-epi and reuse the parent wafer as a fresh substrate.
why: Grinding wastes ~95% of HBM silicon; spalling recovers it, cutting crystal demand per HBM bit ~5-10x and attacking the 3x wafer-area HBM tax on the materials side.

title: Eliminate the quartz crucible: cold-crucible skull-melt Czochralski growth
idea: Melt silicon inside a water-cooled, segmented copper crucible heated by induction so a frozen silicon skull is the only surface touching the melt, then pull the crystal from that self-contained melt and add oxygen deliberately by controlled O2/SiO gas doping to keep gettering behaviour.
why: Removes the single-use Spruce Pine high-purity quartz crucible (>80% concentrated) consumed by every 300 mm ingot, and crucible-borne contamination.

title: DRAM's own capacitor forest replaces package decoupling MLCCs
idea: Combine the cell-capacitor process with power-delivery decoupling: the one added mask shorts blocks of storage capacitors in periphery gaps and die corners into on-die decaps (>1 uF/mm2, since 5 fF per ~900 nm2 cell), deleting most BaTiO3/Ni MLCCs and tantalum capacitors on HBM and DIMM substrates.
why: Sidesteps recurring MLCC and tantalum (DRC) shortages; quieter supply lets VDD margin drop ~5%, a direct CV2 energy cut.

title: Lab-grown diamond glut repurposed as HBM thermal interlayers
idea: Lab-grown jewelry diamonds have crashed in price as CVD reactor capacity floods the market. Point those reactors at thin polycrystalline diamond wafers (~1,500 W/m-K) bonded to the HBM base die and top core die as lateral heat spreaders, with extra die thinning to keep the standard stack height; JEDEC HBM pinout and protocol are untouched.
why: Lowers peak stack temperature ~10-15 C so more of the stack stays below 85 C and avoids 2x refresh (refresh costs 10-20% of bandwidth), using spare non-chokepoint diamond-grower capacity.

title: Fluorocarbon-free chlorine etch with tapered, error-tolerated pillars
idea: Reverse the anisotropy priority: etch capacitor and contact holes in HBr/Cl2/O2 pulsed plasmas with no fluorocarbons, accept the tapered profiles that leave ~1% weak cells, and correct them with ECC.
why: Eliminates PFAS-class C4F8/C4F6/CHF3 process gases (regulatory and supply risk) from the heaviest etch steps.

title: Coulomb-blockade silicon nanodots hold countable electrons in all-silicon cells
idea: Effect: a 5 nm Si nanodot has a charging energy well above kT, so Coulomb blockade adds an escape barrier on top of the SiO2 tunnel barrier. Store ~10-30 electrons by direct tunneling and read them with an adjacent room-temperature single-electron-transistor charge sensor; the cell needs only Si, SiO2 and doped-Si wiring.
why: Removes the capacitor (facts 1-2), high-k and W; the tiny stored charge gives ~100x lower CV2 write energy.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor foil anodizing makes self-ordered capacitor holes
idea: Aluminum electrolytic-capacitor makers grow porous alumina by anodizing foil; deposit a thick Al film over the access-transistor layer, pre-texture it with a shallow imprint at the landing-pad pitch, and anodize in sulfuric acid at low voltage to grow ordered 40-60 nm pitch pores registered to the texture, then line them with TiN/ZrO2/TiN.
why: Replaces the deepest fluorocarbon plasma etch and its hard-mask stack with a room-temperature wet electrochemical step on abundant aluminum; anodic alumina routinely exceeds 115:1, attacking the capacitor charge wall while cutting PFAS etch gas and etcher energy.

title: Substitute atomic hydrogen radicals for sulfuric-peroxide resist strips
idea: Strip implant-hardened photoresist with downstream remote-plasma atomic hydrogen followed by a short UV-ozone polish, replacing SPM (piranha) baths and their hot DI rinses.
why: SPM strip and rinse is among the highest water and sulfuric-acid consumers per step; the dry strip cuts water >10x and eliminates the sulfuric acid supply chain for it.

title: Substitute phosphate-fertilizer fluorosilicic acid for imported fluorspar
idea: Recover fluorosilicic acid already scrubbed at Florida and Idaho phosphate plants, convert it to anhydrous HF through the ammonium bifluoride route, then distill to electronic-grade HF and NF3 feedstock.
why: Fab fluorine chemistry (HF cleans, NF3 chamber cleans, etch gases) rests on Chinese/Mexican fluorspar; this domestic byproduct stream could cover most US fab fluorine demand.

title: U.S. fluorine from phosphate-fertilizer fluorosilicic acid waste
idea: Worsen: buy the fluorine behind HF, NF3 and WF6 from Chinese and Mexican fluorspar. Flip: capture the fluorosilicic acid (H2SiF6) already scrubbed at Florida and Louisiana phosphate plants, convert it to anhydrous HF plus high-purity silica, and feed domestic electronic-grade NF3/HF plants.
why: Fluorspar chokepoint and U.S. manufacturability: phosphate byproduct fluorine is many times fab demand, and the silica co-product has its own value.

title: Machine-shop carbide scrap becomes domestic tungsten hexafluoride
idea: Scale jump from industrial tooling to semiconductor gas: collect U.S. cemented-carbide scrap (drills, inserts; thousands of t/yr) and recover tungsten by the zinc process or oxidation to WO3. An existing U.S. chemical plant then fluorinates it to electronic-grade WF6.
why: Builds a domestic closed loop around the ~80%-Chinese tungsten chokepoint. Fab WF6 demand is only hundreds of tonnes, far below the scrap available.

title: Hall-Heroult for silicon: molten-salt electrowinning from sand
idea: Aluminum is won by electrolysis in molten salt; reduce silica pellets electrochemically in molten CaCl2 at ~850 C (FFC-style) or electrodeposit silicon from silica dissolved in chloride melts onto silicon cathodes, then zone-refine the product to electronic grade.
why: Bypasses carbothermic metallurgical silicon (coke electrodes, 11-13 kWh/kg) and the Siemens trichlorosilane process (~50-60 kWh/kg) and its chlorosilane chemistry, cutting feedstock energy by ~50% or more.

title: Nanoimprint DRAM: let the code eat the template defects
idea: Pattern critical DRAM layers by nanoimprint (no EUV, no light source) and stop fighting its defect density: imprint-induced particle and pinch defects (~1% of cells at worst) are mapped at test and corrected by on-die ECC.
why: NIL failed for DRAM mainly on defectivity; tolerating 1% BER removes that blocker and replaces EUV ($200M+ tools, one supplier) with ~10x cheaper, lower-power imprint tools.

title: Indium-free zinc-tin-silicon oxide gain cell with graded self-insulator
idea: Combine channel and gate insulator in one co-sputtered Zn-Sn-Si-O film whose Si fraction ramps from ~5% (semiconducting channel) to ~50% (amorphous insulator) in a single chamber pass, forming a 2T gain-cell storage transistor with no indium, no gallium and no separate gate-oxide ALD.
why: IGZO gain cells depend on indium (China ~60%) and gallium (China ~98%, export-controlled); ZTSO uses abundant Zn, Sn, Si and one deposition replaces two while keeping wide-bandgap ultra-low leakage.

title: Subtractive molybdenum bitlines with self-aligned air-gap spacers
idea: Combine bitline patterning with spacer formation (zero added masks, existing bitline mask): blanket Mo is etched subtractively in Cl2/O2, then a non-conformal cap pinches off over the gaps, leaving k=1 air spacers.
why: Tungsten-free bitline from U.S.-mined Mo; ~30% lower bitline capacitance gives more sense signal or longer bitlines (fewer sense amps) and lower CV2 energy per access.

title: Solderless copper-to-copper bonded stacks immune to intermetallic growth
idea: Minify the bond to 3 um-pitch direct Cu-Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonds in memory stacks, eliminating SnAg microbumps and organic underfill.
why: No tin, silver or underfill, and no Kirkendall voiding or intermetallic growth over 10 years at 125 C; also raises stack density and shrinks TSV keep-out (fact 6).

title: Intaglio acid-etching: catalytic metal etch carves 115:1 silicon trenches
idea: Printmakers bite intaglio plates with acid only where the ground is scratched away; metal-assisted chemical etching does the same in silicon: a patterned silver mesh sinks straight down in HF/H2O2, carving capacitor holes in a sacrificial silicon mold at >150:1, after which the silver is recovered electrochemically and the mold is oxidized or replaced.
why: Reaches the AR ~115 needed for more Cs without C4F6/C4F8 plasma (PFAS, high GWP) or high-power RF etchers, near room temperature; silver is recycled in a closed loop.

title: Refinery fluid-catalytic-cracking reactors become the polysilicon template
idea: Oil refiners run fluidized-bed reactors continuously with particles suspended in gas. Restart and scale U.S. fluidized-bed granular polysilicon (silane decomposed on heated seed granules) to semiconductor purity, giving ~80-90% lower deposition energy than Siemens rods and free-flowing granules that feed continuous-recharge Czochralski pullers.
why: Cuts the energy of the most power-hungry input (Siemens ~50-60 kWh/kg) and builds a non-Chinese domestic feedstock; granular recharge also lets one crucible yield several ingots.

title: Aluminum-induced layer exchange grows poly-silicon access transistors at 350 C
idea: Effect: amorphous Si dissolves into Al grain boundaries and crystallizes underneath at ~350 C, swapping layer order (layer exchange) to give >10 um grains with no Ni, laser or furnace. Strip the Al, thin and counter-dope the film, and build stacked BEOL access and periphery transistors over the array.
why: Single-crystal wafer intensity (quartz crucibles, polysilicon) and 3D tier cost (fact 2): extra silicon tiers come from abundant Al and silane under 400 C.

title: HVAC-technician tracer gas: hydrogen/nitrogen leak checks replace helium
idea: HVAC and automotive leak technicians use 5% H2 in N2 with palladium sniffers because it is cheap and needs no helium. Requalify vacuum-tool leak checking in a university fab using forming-gas tracer, H2-selective sensors and an RGA tuned to mass 2, and document a minimum detectable leak of ~1e-7 mbar-L/s.
why: Removes a recurring helium use at near-zero cost while supply is disrupted, with a procedure fabs can copy.

title: Copper heap-leach mining: bacteria recover tungsten, hafnium, ruthenium from scrap
idea: Copper miners bioleach low-grade ore with Acidithiobacillus. Run stirred bioreactors where acidophilic and siderophore-producing microbes leach W, Hf, Zr, Ru and Ta from scrapped wafers, spent sputter targets, chamber shields and test boards at ambient temperature, followed by solvent extraction to reagent grade.
why: Turns fab scrap and e-waste into a domestic secondary source of chokepoint refractory metals without smelters; target 30-50% of fab refractory-metal demand from recycled feed at low energy.

title: Po the fab never etches: bottom-up area-selective capacitor growth
idea: Po: 'the fab is forbidden to etch.' Extracted: grow capacitor pillars bottom-up by area-selective deposition, with inhibitor monolayers blocking growth on the oxide field while TiN or Mo grows only on exposed storage-node plugs, re-dosing the inhibitor every few nanometers to reach AR 60+. This removes the high-aspect-ratio fluorocarbon mold etch.
why: PFAS and fluorinated-gas intensity (the high-AR mold etch is a major C4F6/C4F8/NF3 consumer, GWP >7000) and etch-tool capex; also eliminates mold-collapse yield loss.

title: Overspray recovery: capture and re-refine ALD precursors from exhaust
idea: Paint booths reclaim overspray; fit ALD and CVD forelines with cold-finger condensers and chelating sorbent cartridges that capture unreacted Zr, Hf, Ru, Mo and W organometallics and halides, then return the cartridges to a precursor refinery that strips and redistills them.
why: ALD sends 90-99% of metal precursor to the abatement burner; closing the loop could halve new hafnium, zirconium and ruthenium demand and cut abatement fuel.

title: Optical-fiber soot process makes domestic photomask blanks, recycled like cullet
idea: Use New York flame-hydrolysis high-purity fused silica (the soot method behind optical-fiber preforms) as mask substrate, and add a cullet-style reclaim line that strips chrome, repolishes and recoats retired DRAM masks for reuse.
why: Mask blanks are concentrated in Japan; a U.S. source plus 3-5 reuse cycles per blank cuts synthetic-quartz demand and mask cost for the ~60-70 masks a DRAM product needs.

title: Core memory rethreaded by lithography: microtoroids around through-glass vias
idea: Magnetic core memory died on hand-threading labor and millimeter cores, not on its materials (iron oxide ferrite and copper). On glass panels, laser-drill via arrays, electroplate copper X, Y and sense lines through them, and form 5-10 um ferrite or NiFe rings around each crossing by room-temperature aerosol deposition, writing by coincident current.
why: Only iron oxide, Zn/Mn/Ni, copper and glass: no chokepoint input; infinite endurance and nonvolatile, so no refresh; ~1 GB/m2 per layer at 10 um pitch, so best for rad-hard or infinite-write tiers unless rings shrink further.

title: Chlorination plus ligand-exchange thermal ALE for 3D DRAM lateral recess
idea: Periodic-table walk, Cl (17): recess TiN, ZrO2 and Al2O3 laterally inside 3D DRAM tiers by cyclic thermal atomic-layer etching, chlorinating with SOCl2 or BCl3 then removing the surface with TiCl4 or trimethylaluminum ligand exchange, avoiding the HF step of standard thermal ALE.
why: Self-limiting, isotropic, angstrom-precise cavities across 100+ tiers (fact 2 blocker), fluorine-free.

title: Sputter-free fab: every liner, barrier and electrode by thermal ALD
idea: Box [ALD TiN/ZrO2 cap | Si | voltage SA | standard | Si | thermal ALD/CVD with N2 carriers + NH3/H2 reducers + remote NH3/NF3 pre-clean]: requalify every Ar-sputtered film (Ti/TiN contact liners, bitline metal, silicide seed, periphery gate metal) and every Ar sputter pre-clean as gas-phase thermal processes.
why: Removes argon from deposition entirely; the constraint also forces near-100% step coverage, which 3D DRAM tiers and high-AR contacts need anyway.

title: Tin-oxide spacers etched by hydrogen for fluorine-free multiple patterning
idea: Periodic-table walk, Sn (50): use ALD SnO2 as the SADP/SAQP spacer and hardmask, etched in H2/CH4 plasma (volatile SnH4) with high selectivity to Si, SiO2 and carbon, while Si and carbon are etched in Cl2/HBr/O2, a full pitch-quartering flow without CF chemistry; Sn is reclaimed from exhaust.
why: Removes CF4/CHF3 spacer etches and lets DUV SAQP displace some of the 5-7 EUV layers (single-supplier chokepoint).

title: Wartime salvage drive for DRAM: harvest chips from retired servers
idea: Revive WWII scrap-salvage logistics for memory: collect DDR4/DDR5 modules from decommissioned servers, robotically desolder and re-ball the packages, burn-in and retest them, and rebuild them onto CXL memory-expander cards pooled as a slower tier.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: millions of server DIMMs are shredded every year, and reuse adds supply with zero wafers, helium or quartz; claims several percent of annual bit demand.

title: Hafnium- and zirconium-free titania capacitors with a corrected leakage tail
idea: Swap ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 for abundant TiO2/Al2O3 nanolaminates (k~40-60) and treat the ~1% of cells with grain-boundary leakage as correctable erasures flagged by a retention-profiling map.
why: Removes Zr/Hf (zircon byproduct supply, nuclear-grade separation) from the capacitor using earth-abundant Ti, with equal or higher Cs per area.

title: Slot-die sol-gel zinc-tin-oxide gain cells patterned on logic BEOL
idea: Box [charge on read-TFT gate | 2T0C ZnSnO TFTs | current sense | BEOL monolithic over CMOS | logic wafer | aqueous nitrate sol-gel slot-die coat + NIL patterning + 265 nm UV-LED assisted 300 C cure in air]: coat ZnSnO channel and AlOx gate-dielectric inks at atmospheric pressure, with no vacuum, no sputter targets and no lamps.
why: Ga/In-free (Zn and Sn are abundant) and sputter-free oxide gain cells: leakage <1e-18 A gives seconds of retention, so refresh falls ~100x, with no IGZO targets or Ar plasma.

title: Snowflake: 77 K DRAM shrinks capacitor and drops high-k
idea: Stimulus 'snowflake' (cold preserves delicate structure) -> run DRAM arrays in liquid-nitrogen-cooled racks where junction and subthreshold leakage fall by >10^4, so retention stays long with Cs ~1 fF; that permits a short, low-AR capacitor with plain Al2O3/SiO2 dielectric instead of ZrO2/HfO2.
why: Removes high-k (Hf/Zr) and the deepest fluorocarbon etch and nearly eliminates refresh energy; LN2 comes from air, with cooling energy as the trade-off.

title: Manganese oxide abrasive replaces rare-earth ceria in CMP
idea: TRIZ #38 Strong oxidants: use Mn2O3/MnO2 nanoparticles whose Mn3+/Mn4+ redox bonds to and breaks Si-O bonds, supplying the 'chemical tooth' that ceria provides via Ce3+/Ce4+. They replace ceria in STI and ILD planarization.
why: Removes ceria (a China-dominated rare earth) from DRAM's heavy STI/ILD CMP load. Mn is ~950 ppm in the crust and can be refined in the U.S.

title: Archerfish jet printing of photoresist instead of spin coating
idea: Archerfish shoot shaped water jets that focus on a target. Replace spin coating with a multi-nozzle jet printhead that lays resist, BARC and spin-on carbon only on the wafer at the needed thickness, followed by a brief solvent-vapour reflow to level the film.
why: Spin coating wastes ~90-95% of dispensed resist; jetting cuts resist and fluorinated PAG use ~10x, along with solvent waste.

title: Cultured-quartz program revived: fully synthetic silica crucibles from SiCl4
idea: Copy the WWII Signal Corps/Bell Labs move that replaced Brazilian natural quartz with hydrothermally cultured crystal: make the whole Czochralski crucible, not just its inner layer, from flame-hydrolysed synthetic silica soot made from silicon tetrachloride, a by-product of US polysilicon plants.
why: Breaks the Spruce Pine (>80%) chokepoint for high-purity quartz crucibles and turns a waste stream into feedstock; claims full crucible supply independence for US wafer makers.

title: Plasma-catalytic PFC conversion returns fluorine as reusable HF
idea: Worsen: burn PFC exhaust in natural-gas abatement and dump the fluoride as CaF2 sludge. Flip: use plasma-catalytic abatement to convert CF4/NF3/SF6 to HF, capture it as clean HF in a wet column, and ship it back to the NF3/HF supplier as feedstock in returnable totes.
why: Fluorspar and fluorine-gas supply: closes ~50% of the fluorine loop and cuts PFC emissions.

title: Architectural-glass rotary magnetrons cut sputter-target metal waste
idea: Architectural glass coaters use rotating cylindrical targets that erode evenly to ~80-90% utilization versus ~30-40% for planar racetrack targets. Adapt dual rotary-cathode PVD with a scanning 300 mm pedestal for W/Mo, Ti/TiN and Ta liners and re-spray spent tubes; the film stacks are identical, so DDR/HBM dies are unchanged.
why: Cuts purchased tungsten, tantalum and titanium per wafer by roughly half with identical films, and fewer target swaps raise tool uptime.

title: Self-ordering anodic alumina pores as lithography-free capacitor molds
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero EUV and zero plasma for the capacitor layer. Deposit thick aluminum over the storage-node contacts, nanoimprint shallow pits on the contact grid, and anodize in sulfuric or oxalic acid so pores self-organize at the pits and grow straight to AR >100; open the barrier oxide at the bottom and fill with electrode and dielectric.
why: Replaces 1-2 EUV or multipatterning masks and the hardest dry etch with a room-temperature electrochemical step using abundant aluminum; capacitor AR is set only by film thickness.

title: Reclaimed monitor wafers reborn under thick device-grade epitaxy
idea: Combine wafer reclaim with epitaxy (zero masks): repolish reclaimed monitor and prime-reject wafers, grow a 3-5 um device-grade epi layer, and add a backside polysilicon gettering layer to replace oxygen-precipitate gettering.
why: Monitor/test wafers are ~10-20% of fab wafer use; turning them into product substrates cuts virgin wafer, crucible and polysilicon demand ~10-15% and epi lowers the defect-driven leakage tail.

title: Child at the beach: sand-memory shadow behind every DRAM cell
idea: Persona: a child who makes a backup of the sandcastle. Pair each 1T1C cell with a tiny silicon-rich SiOx resistive element on its storage-node contact. The element is written only at power-down, copying the charge state into a filament, and read back at power-up, so it needs thousands of cycles, not 1e16.
why: Non-volatile DRAM made with only Si and O, no Ta or Hf oxides, that keeps DRAM speed and unlimited endurance in normal operation. Area cost ~10-20%.

title: DRAM as lossy mirror of flash: refetch instead of protect
idea: Reverse which copy is authoritative: for clean (read-mostly) pages such as model weights and file cache, a cheap checksum detects errors on reject-grade 1%-BER dies and the line is refetched from the SSD copy.
why: Lets low-grade dies serve large read-mostly footprints, adding usable capacity without new wafers.

title: Stencil shadow-mask deposition revived: no resist, no etch, no PFAS
idea: Revive 1960s shadow-mask evaporation with MEMS silicon-nitride stencils held close to the wafer, depositing patterned metals and dielectrics directly for BEOL plates, pads and periphery wiring with no resist and no etch.
why: No EUV, no PFAS resists or etch gases, and almost no chemical waste; claims 3-5 mask-and-etch modules removed per wafer.

title: Eliminate vacuum pumps: atmospheric spatial ALD for capacitor dielectrics
idea: A gas-bearing spatial ALD head separates precursor zones with N2 curtains at atmospheric pressure while the wafer moves beneath it; pulsed-pressure dwell cycles push precursor down high-AR holes.
why: Drops dry pumps (a major share of deposition-tool energy), raises throughput 5-10x and cuts precursor waste; conformality at 70:1 is the open question.

title: Rotating cylindrical tungsten and titanium targets triple sputter utilization
idea: Scale transfer from display-glass coaters to wafer tools: planar PVD targets erode in a racetrack groove and are scrapped at ~25-35% use. A compact rotary cylindrical magnetron adapted to 300 mm chambers erodes the target evenly to ~80%.
why: ~2.5x less tungsten, titanium and target-bonding material per wafer, plus fewer target-change downtimes.

title: Substitute an electromagnetic cold crucible for the quartz crucible
idea: Grow CZ ingots from silicon held in a segmented copper cold crucible where induction fields form a thin solid skull and push the melt off the walls; deliver the interstitial oxygen DRAM needs for intrinsic gettering by metering SiO/O2 into the argon cover gas instead of dissolving a fused-quartz crucible.
why: Eliminates the >80% Spruce Pine high-purity-quartz crucible dependence per ingot; gas-metered oxygen gives axially uniform oxygen precipitates and tighter retention-tail gettering.

title: Laser-crystallized polysilicon tiers: grain boundaries accepted for 3D
idea: Rearrange display technology into memory: stack 3D DRAM tiers of excimer- or green-laser-crystallized polysilicon access transistors instead of epitaxial Si/SiGe, accepting ~1% grain-boundary-leaky cells as correctable.
why: Removes germanium, epitaxy and wafer bonding from 3D stacking; each tier is a low-cost deposition plus laser anneal, attacking the 26-tier break-even.

title: Two-beam interference lithography prints the cell grid maskless
idea: Magnify one exposure to the whole periodic array: pattern the perfectly periodic DRAM cell grid with interfering 193 nm beams (standing-wave lithography), and use a cheap DUV trim mask only at array edges.
why: Replaces several EUV or multi-patterning steps, cutting EUV electricity (~1 MW per tool), tin and hydrogen use, and capital (fact 4).

title: Antifouling-paint copper oxide and varistor zinc oxide form oxide SRAM
idea: Marine antifouling paint consumes Cu2O by the kiloton, and surge arresters use ZnO. Adapt p-type Cu2O and n-type ZnO thin-film transistors into a complementary BEOL latch: a static 4T/6T cell stacked in multiple tiers over logic.
why: Refresh-free bits with no capacitor and no indium, from abundant Cu and Zn oxides; multi-tier stacking recovers density. The risks are Cu2O hole mobility and off-current.

title: Separable-liner quartz crucibles recycled into new inner layers
idea: Worsen: break and landfill every CZ crucible after one pull. Flip: design crucibles with a separable high-purity inner liner, then crush spent liners, strip the devitrified cristobalite and metal-rich skin by hot chlorination and HF leach, and re-fuse the purified grain into new liners.
why: HPQ Spruce Pine chokepoint: recovering ~50-60% of liner mass roughly halves virgin HPQ need.

title: Po wafers give birth: porous-silicon reusable parent wafer
idea: Po: 'a wafer is a mother that gives birth to daughters.' Extracted: anodize a double-porosity layer on a parent wafer, grow a 20-50 um device-quality epitaxial film on it, build the DRAM, bond to a carrier and split at the weak porous layer; re-polish and reuse the parent 10-20 times.
why: Crucible, polysilicon and ingot energy per DRAM wafer cut ~10x; the thin film also eases thermal management and die stacking.

title: Flip the gate under: substrate-doped buried wordline replaces tungsten
idea: Rearrange the stack so the wordline is below the channel: an epitaxially grown, heavily doped n+ silicon line in the substrate acts as back gate under a thin vertical or planar channel, eliminating the recessed buried-tungsten wordline.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6 from the wordline, the largest W use in a DRAM cell; trades some RC for supply security and a simpler fill-free process.

title: Hardmask becomes the wordline: keep the TiN, skip tungsten
idea: Rearrange roles of patterning and function: the TiN hardmask that defines the recessed gate trench is left in place and thickened as the gate metal, with shorter wordline segments driven by more local drivers to compensate RC.
why: Removes a strip step, a W fill and its WF6/NF3 chemistry; titanium is abundant and widely sourced, cutting W content of the array to near zero.

title: Thirty-two-cell local bitlines shrink the storage capacitor tenfold
idea: Signal is dV = Vcell*Cs/(Cs+CBL): a ~50 fF bitline forces ~5 fF cells, but a local two-transistor sense stage every 32 cells (CBL ~3 fF) yields the same ~100 mV from ~0.5 fF, so the capacitor becomes a shallow AR~7 cup.
why: Deletes the AR 60-75 mold etch (fluorocarbon gas, etch tools) and ~90% of ZrO2/TiN ALD material per bit, at the cost of more sense-amp area.

title: Refrigerant HFO transition applied to high-aspect-ratio etch chemistry
idea: Air conditioning moved from high-GWP HFCs to short-lived hydrofluoroolefins (HFO-1234ze/yf). Requalify capacitor-hole and contact etches on unsaturated fluorocarbons (C4F6 isomers, HFO-1234ze, CF3I) whose C=C bonds deposit sidewall polymer at lower flow, combined with point-of-use plasma abatement.
why: Cuts the GWP of etch emissions >90% and pre-empts PFAS/F-gas restrictions that could choke C4F8/CF4 supply, while keeping HAR selectivity for 60-75:1 pillars.

title: Supercritical CO2 with ozone replaces water rinse-and-dry cycles
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics and hydraulics: clean and dry wafers in pressurized supercritical CO2 carrying dissolved ozone and a little alcohol co-solvent, then recompress and reuse the CO2.
why: Cuts UPW and IPA use. Zero surface tension also ends pillar collapse, so taller capacitors become possible (fact 1); only C, O and H are involved.

title: Kerfless laser-split wafering of DRAM-grade silicon ingots
idea: Ideal: slicing with zero sawdust. Closest: focus an IR picosecond laser inside the ingot to write a sub-surface modified plane (KABRA-style, proven on SiC), then split each wafer off by thermal/ultrasonic stress; kerf drops from ~150 um to ~20 um and lapping shrinks.
why: ~30-40% more wafers per ingot, cutting polysilicon, quartz crucibles, puller energy, slurry and water per wafer proportionally.

title: MLCC core-shell titanate grains for an abundant high-k capacitor
idea: Multilayer ceramic capacitor makers flatten BaTiO3 permittivity with core-shell grains (a ferroelectric core inside a doped paraelectric shell). Adapt this as an ALD nanolaminate of SrTiO3 cores with Ba/Mg-doped shells on a TiO2-templated TiN electrode to reach k ~70-100 in a 6 nm film.
why: Fact 1 says k ~70 is needed. Titanates use abundant Ba/Sr/Ti instead of Hf/Zr and let pillar aspect ratio fall from ~70:1 toward ~40:1, cutting deep-etch fluorocarbon gas and helium-cooled etch time.

title: Self-passivated chamber walls eliminate NF3 cleans for ALD and CVD
idea: ALD/CVD films grow only where precursors find reactive sites; keep chamber walls and liners capped with a renewable small-molecule inhibitor re-dosed each lot and held above the precursor desorption temperature, so walls never accumulate film and periodic NF3 remote-plasma cleans disappear.
why: NF3 (GWP ~16,000) chamber cleaning is a top fab fluorochemical and greenhouse consumer; ~70-80% cut plus ~5-10% more tool uptime.

title: $1-IoT zinc-tin-oxide gain cells, indium and gallium free
idea: Disposable $1 IoT tags push oxide transistors toward the cheapest metals. Sputter amorphous Zn-Sn-O (ZTO) as the channel of 2T0C gain cells with ALD Al2O3 gate dielectric and Al or Mo electrodes, annealed below 350 C in a university fab.
why: IGZO gain cells (prior work) depend on indium (China ~60%) and export-controlled gallium; ZTO uses abundant Zn and Sn while aiming for the ~1e-19 A off-current needed for long retention (fact 3).

title: Indium- and gallium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain-cell transistor
idea: Periodic-table walk, Zn (30): replace IGZO in 2T0C gain cells with amorphous Zn-Sn-O (Zn:Sn ~2:1) by ALD (diethylzinc + TDMA-Sn), with Si or Al doping to pin oxygen vacancies for <1e-19 A/um off-current.
why: Removes Ga (~98% China primary) and In (~60% China) from capacitor-less oxide DRAM; two abundant metals only.

title: Strontium-catalyzed native-oxide desorption replaces the HF-last clean
idea: Periodic-table walk, Sr (38): before epitaxy or gate stacks, deposit ~0.5 monolayer Sr in vacuum and anneal at ~750-800 C; Sr reduces SiO2 to volatile SiO plus SrO and leaves an oxide-free (2x1) surface, borrowing the SrTiO3-on-Si MBE trick.
why: Removes the HF dip on which every front-end clean depends, plus its rinse water.

title: Washing machine: endpoint sensors stop rinses when wafers are clean
idea: Stimulus 'washing machine' (rinse cycles run fixed times regardless) -> a 10-person team builds retrofit in-line resistivity/TOC sensors and controllers for wet benches that end each rinse when effluent matches incoming UPW, replacing fixed-time recipes.
why: Wet benches are the largest UPW users; endpoint rinsing cuts UPW and UPW-production energy ~25-40%.

title: Aluminum metal-last wordlines replacing tungsten
idea: Reverse metallization order: form wordlines with a sacrificial nitride, finish all high-temperature steps, then replace it with abundant aluminum by low-temperature CVD; voids and electromigration opens (~1% of cells) are corrected by row-erasure coding.
why: Removes tungsten from the wordline using U.S.-producible aluminum, with lower resistivity than W at relaxed widths.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching drills capacitor holes without plasma
idea: Worsen: etch every capacitor hole with fluorocarbon plasma (C4F6/C4F8) in $10M+ tools that struggle past AR 70. Flip: pattern a porous Ag or Au catalyst mesh and use metal-assisted chemical etching (HF/H2O2) to sink vertical holes into a silicon mold at AR >100 in a wet bath, then convert the mold to oxide or replace it.
why: PFAS-class etch gases, etch tool capital and the AR ~115 capacitor target: wet-bath capex is ~10x lower and MacEtch has shown AR >100.

title: Po the crystal draws the pattern: facet-defined sub-litho fins
idea: Po: 'the crystal is the lithographer.' Extracted: on (110) silicon, TMAH wet etch stops on vertical {111} planes, so a coarse 40 nm DUV pattern yields atomically flat vertical walls; self-limiting oxidation then thins fins to 8-10 nm, giving access-transistor fins and buried-wordline trenches without EUV.
why: EUV single-supplier chokepoint (5-7 EUV layers): replaces 2-3 EUV layers with DUV plus wet chemistry, and the wet etch avoids fluorinated plasma gases.

title: Eliminate the half-VDD precharge: single-ended precharge-to-ground sensing
idea: Bitlines rest at 0 V and only cells storing 1 lift their bitline, which a current-mirror sense amp compares against a reference cell; restore drives only the 1s, with no VBLP generator or equalization, and data are bit-plane encoded to be mostly zeros.
why: Bitline energy scales with the count of 1 bits; bit-plane encoded AI data at ~90% zeros gives up to ~10x lower array energy per access.

title: Assay campaign for second-source U.S. quartz pegmatites
idea: Within $1M/24 months: core and assay candidate pegmatites (Black Hills, Maine, Georgia) for low-Al/Ti/alkali quartz, run hot-chlorination and flotation purification trials, and make test crucible billets with partner crucible makers.
why: One qualified second U.S. HPQ source breaks the single-valley (>80%) chokepoint; the budget covers drilling and lab purification.

title: Woodworm: metal-assisted chemical etching bores capacitor holes plasma-free
idea: Stimulus 'woodworm' (a tiny creature bores straight tunnels) -> pattern an Ag or Pt catalyst mesh, then etch in HF/H2O2 at room temperature; the catalyst sinks vertically and bores AR >100 holes in sacrificial silicon that become the capacitor mold.
why: Replaces fluorocarbon (PFAS) plasma and costly high-AR etch tools, and lets AR pass 100 to break the capacitor charge wall.

title: Swimming-pool ozone chemistry replaces sulfuric-peroxide resist strip
idea: Pools and bottling plants sanitize with dissolved ozone instead of harsh chemicals. Strip photoresist and organics with high-concentration ozonated UPW (>80 ppm, with UV assist and CO2 spiking to protect surfaces) in a university wet bench, benchmarking against SPM on implanted resist.
why: SPM consumes large volumes of sulfuric acid, peroxide and rinse water; ozone is made from oxygen on demand, cutting chemical purchases and wastewater ~80%.

title: Monolayer MoS2 channels collapse 3D tier pitch to twenty nanometers
idea: Tier pitch = channel + 2x dielectric + gate + isolation; a 0.65 nm MoS2 monolayer (Eg 1.8 eV, no dangling bonds, low off-leakage) replaces a 10-20 nm Si channel, shrinking tiers from ~50 to ~20 nm. Grow MoS2 per tier by low-temperature MOCVD.
why: A fixed 5 um etchable stack holds 250 tiers instead of 100; with a relaxed lateral cell that is ~10x density at the same etch/litho cost. Mo and S are US-abundant; W-based TMDs avoided.

title: Boron-carbon hardmask replaces tungsten-doped carbon for deep etches
idea: Periodic-table walk, B (5): PECVD boron-rich carbon (30-60% B from B2H6 plus C3H6) gives B-C bonds whose etch resistance rivals W-doped carbon in high-aspect-ratio etches, and it strips in O2/Cl2.
why: Removes W from hardmasks for capacitor and contact etches; the U.S. is a top-two borate producer.

title: Rusting aluminum: anodic alumina self-orders capacitor holes without EUV
idea: Stimulus 'rust' (corrosion that builds structure) -> anodize an aluminum film in oxalic/phosphoric acid so it self-organizes into a hexagonal array of straight nanopores (~25-60 nm pitch, AR >100), registered by a light DUV pre-pattern; use the pores as the capacitor mold, ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN, then dissolve the alumina.
why: Replaces 1-2 EUV layers and the C4F6/C4F8 high-AR plasma etch with a wet electrochemical bath; AR >100 is native, attacking the capacitor charge wall and fluorocarbon/PFAS use.

title: On-die memory passport logs wear, faults and material content
idea: Worsen: give every chip no history, so recyclers must assume it is junk. Flip: reserve a small OTP/eFuse region where the chip logs total activations, ECC corrections, repairs and a bill-of-materials hash, readable by a standard command, so graders can price and route reuse in seconds.
why: Makes reuse and material recovery pay: grading cost falls ~10x and the reuse rate rises.

title: Supercritical-CO2 drying to push capacitor pillars past AR 100
idea: Periodic-table walk, C+O (6,8): perform post-etch rinse and dry in supercritical CO2 with a non-fluorinated co-solvent, removing the liquid meniscus whose capillary force topples 60-75:1 pillars, and recover CO2 from industrial streams.
why: Direct attack on the capacitor charge wall (AR ~115 needed), plus less water and IPA.

title: PFAS-free nonstick cookware chemistry for immersion topcoats and resists
idea: Cookware makers replaced PTFE with sol-gel ceramic silica nonstick coatings. Replace fluoropolymer immersion-lithography topcoats with hydrophobic alkyl-silsesquioxane sol-gel topcoats and swap perfluoroalkyl-sulfonate photoacid generators for non-fluorinated sulfonium-carboxylate or metal-oxide resists; process-only, DDR/HBM output unchanged.
why: Coming EU/U.S. PFAS restrictions could choke fluorinated litho chemicals used on every DUV layer; this removes that regulatory supply risk and fluorinated wastewater.

title: Dry fab: skip non-critical cleans, let particles become correctable bits
idea: Rearrange where cleanliness is enforced: delete ~half of post-CMP/post-etch wet cleans on non-critical layers and accept the resulting particle-induced cell defects, held below 1% BER and corrected on-die.
why: Ultrapure water and chemical use per wafer down ~40-60%, plus fewer tool steps, which eases water-limited U.S. siting.

title: Molting crucible: spray-printed silica cuticle on a reusable shell
idea: Crabs shed and rebuild a thin cuticle on the same body. Keep a reusable silicon-nitride-coated graphite or SiC crucible body and spray-print a fresh 1-2 mm synthetic silica cuticle inside it before each Cz pull, peeling it out with the residual melt after cooling.
why: Cuts high-purity quartz per ingot ~80-90% and makes synthetic silica practical for crucibles, attacking the Spruce Pine >80% chokepoint.

title: Harvest helium and neon from the fab's own nitrogen plant
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging: a mega-fab's on-site air-separation unit already processes ~100k Nm3/h of air for nitrogen. Add a non-condensable stripping column and a small cryo-adsorber that co-produce crude Ne (18 ppm in air) and He (5 ppm), then purify both on site, so rare-gas production merges into a plant the fab already runs.
why: Makes neon (litho lasers, a Ukraine-exposed supply) and part of the helium a domestic byproduct: a few thousand Nm3/yr of He and ~10k Nm3/yr of Ne per fab ASU, covering laser gas and leak checking.

title: Solid-state 193 nm light: lithography without neon gas
idea: Reverse the laser medium: replace ArF excimer gas discharge with frequency-converted fiber/solid-state lasers (e.g., sum-frequency mixing to 193 nm) as DUV scanner sources.
why: Removes neon, xenon and fluorine refill gases (Ukraine/Russia neon chokepoint) and their purification energy; better wall-plug efficiency.
